# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_config_reference.py — do not edit by hand. -->

Every environment variable the backend reads. Regenerate with
`venv/bin/python scripts/gen_config_reference.py`;
`tests/unit/core/test_configReference.py` fails while this file is stale.

Locally the values come from `.secrets.toml` (section chosen by `APP_ENV`);
in the container from `docker/prod.env`, whose commented template is
`docker/prod.env.example`. Secrets are marked **secret**: never commit them,
never log them.

## Application settings (53) — `src/core/config.py`

The description is the comment above the setting in `config.py`; read it
there for the full reasoning.

| Variable | Required | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ENCRYPTION_KEY` **secret** | required | text | — | Key for the Fernet helpers in security/encryption.py. No column is encrypted with it (columns use DATABASE_ENCRYPTION_KEY). |
| `DATABASE_URL` **secret** | required | text | — | Connection URL the app uses — as `noharm_app`, the NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS role, so RLS applies. The entrypoint composes it from the parts below when unset. |
| `DATABASE_HOST` | required | text | — | Database host, used by the entrypoint to compose the URLs. |
| `DATABASE_NAME` | required | text | — | Database name. |
| `DATABASE_USER` | required | text | — | The owner role (superuser in the live compose): migrations, dumps and `rotate-encryption-key` connect as it. Never the app's role. |
| `DATABASE_PASSWORD` **secret** | required | text | — | Password of DATABASE_USER. |
| `DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED` **secret** | required | text | — | Connection URL as the owner role, unpooled — Alembic and the jobs that must bypass RLS. pgBouncer cannot run DDL, hence unpooled. |
| `DATABASE_ENCRYPTION_KEY` **secret** | required | text | — | AES-GCM key for every encrypted column (StringEncryptedType). Losing it makes them unreadable; rotate with `rotate-encryption-key`. Must differ from BLIND_INDEX_KEY. |
| `BLIND_INDEX_KEY` **secret** | required | text | — | Key for the blind indexes (`cl_0b_h`, `cl_0c_h`, `cl_9c_h`) — the lookup columns that make an encrypted username/email/FCM token searchable by exact match. |
| `EXEC_MODE` | required | text | — | `dev` turns on development behaviour (tracebacks in 500s, DEBUG allowed); anything else — `prod`, `test` — is treated as not dev. |
| `DEBUG` | required | boolean | — | Development mode. **Refused at startup unless EXEC_MODE=dev**: Starlette serves its traceback page before any handler when it is on. |
| `PORT` | required | integer | — | Port uvicorn listens on (8080 behind nginx). |
| `STATUS_CODES` | required | JSON | — | The shared status table, JSON: disabled 0, enabled 1, deleted 2, blocked 3, pending 4, accepted 5, ignored 6, unread 7, read 8, banned 9. The front end mirrors it as VITE_STATUS_CONSTANTS. |
| `JWT_SECRET_KEY` **secret** | required | text | — | Signing key for access tokens (15 min). Must differ from JWT_REFRESH_SECRET_KEY, or a refresh token passes as an access token. |
| `JWT_REFRESH_SECRET_KEY` **secret** | required | text | — | Signing key for refresh tokens (7 days). |
| `JWT_ALGORITHM` | required | text | — | JWT algorithm, `HS256`. |
| `ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES` | required | integer | — | Access-token lifetime in minutes (15). |
| `REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRE_DAYS` | required | integer | — | Refresh-token lifetime in days (7). Also how long a 'log out everywhere' cutoff is kept. |
| `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | required | JSON | — | CORS allow-list, JSON. The web build is same-origin; the Capacitor apps need `capacitor://localhost` (iOS) and `https://localhost` (Android, plus `http://localhost` for older builds). |
| `REDIS_URL` | required | text | — | Redis: token blacklist and log-out-everywhere cutoffs, rate limits, quotas, socket presence and connection sets, the admin board cache. |
| `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` **secret** | optional | text | `unset` | The Firebase service-account JSON as one string — verifies ID tokens, sends FCM pushes, deletes Firebase users on purge. |
| `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH` | optional | text | `unset` | Alternative to FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT: a path to the JSON file. |
| `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` | optional | text | `unset` | Only needed when there is no service account to read it from — i.e. the emulator path used by the test suites. Verification matches the token's "aud" and "iss" against this. |
| `TRUSTED_PROXIES` | optional | JSON | `[]` | Peers allowed to set X-Forwarded-For. Plain IPs or CIDR blocks. Deployed, this is the loopback pair and nothing else: nginx runs beside the app in the container and uvicorn binds 127.0.0.1, so the proxy is the only peer that can ever appear. |
| `ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS` | optional | integer | `30` | Deleting an account is a soft delete plus a clock: the row is kept for this many days so the user can sign in again and undo it, and `purge-accounts` destroys it for good once the window closes. |
| `TERMS_VERSION` | optional | text | `"2026-09-28"` | The version of each document the account is currently asked to accept. A consent record stores the version that was live when it was given, and `ConsentService.pending` compares the two — so bumping one of these is what makes every account re-accept, and nothing else has to change. |
| `PRIVACY_VERSION` | optional | text | `"2026-09-28"` | The version of each document the account is currently asked to accept. A consent record stores the version that was live when it was given, and `ConsentService.pending` compares the two — so bumping one of these is what makes every account re-accept, and nothing else has to change. |
| `HEALTH_CONSENT_VERSION` | optional | text | `"1.0"` | Tracked clean days are health data, and health data needs its own explicit, separately given consent — never one bundled into "I agree to the terms". It carries its own version for the same reason it carries its own checkbox: what it covers can change without the terms changing. |
| `ERROR_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` | optional | integer | `90` | Measured from a fault's last sighting, not its birth: a bug first seen in January and still firing today is current. |
| `SUSPICIOUS_WINDOW_SECONDS` | optional | integer | `600` | Suspicious traffic. Counted per client address, failures only, in a window that refreshes while the burst continues. A flag is a prompt to look and never an action: an automatic block driven by these numbers is a denial of service anyone can aim at a shared mobile NAT. |
| `SUSPICIOUS_NOT_FOUND_THRESHOLD` | optional | integer | `40` | Suspicious traffic. Counted per client address, failures only, in a window that refreshes while the burst continues. A flag is a prompt to look and never an action: an automatic block driven by these numbers is a denial of service anyone can aim at a shared mobile NAT. |
| `SUSPICIOUS_AUTH_THRESHOLD` | optional | integer | `20` | Suspicious traffic. Counted per client address, failures only, in a window that refreshes while the burst continues. A flag is a prompt to look and never an action: an automatic block driven by these numbers is a denial of service anyone can aim at a shared mobile NAT. |
| `SUSPICIOUS_SERVER_ERROR_THRESHOLD` | optional | integer | `25` | Suspicious traffic. Counted per client address, failures only, in a window that refreshes while the burst continues. A flag is a prompt to look and never an action: an automatic block driven by these numbers is a denial of service anyone can aim at a shared mobile NAT. |
| `SUSPICIOUS_CLIENT_ERROR_THRESHOLD` | optional | integer | `80` | Suspicious traffic. Counted per client address, failures only, in a window that refreshes while the burst continues. A flag is a prompt to look and never an action: an automatic block driven by these numbers is a denial of service anyone can aim at a shared mobile NAT. |
| `SUSPICIOUS_MAX_KEYS` | optional | integer | `5000` | Suspicious traffic. Counted per client address, failures only, in a window that refreshes while the burst continues. A flag is a prompt to look and never an action: an automatic block driven by these numbers is a denial of service anyone can aim at a shared mobile NAT. |
| `MINIMUM_AGE_YEARS` | optional | integer | `18` | Minimum age to hold an account, in years, checked against the birth date given at registration. |
| `REPORT_EVIDENCE_RETENTION_DAYS` | optional | integer | `180` | How long the copied evidence behind a report is kept after a moderator closed it. The report itself is permanent — it is the record of what was decided about an account — but the evidence is other people's private messages, copied for one purpose, and keeping it past that purpose is a liability rather than a record. |
| `REPORT_LOCK_MINUTES` | optional | integer | `30` | How long a moderator's claim on a report holds before anyone may take it. An expiring lock is the difference between a queue that heals itself and one that fills with reports parked by someone who closed the tab. |
| `REPORT_MAX_PER_HOUR` | optional | integer | `10` | Per-reporter quota, counted only on reports that were actually filed. The per-IP ceiling on the route is the other half: it stops one host hammering the endpoint, this stops one account filing against a hundred different people from a hundred hosts. |
| `REPORT_MAX_PER_DAY` | optional | integer | `30` | Per-reporter quota, counted only on reports that were actually filed. The per-IP ceiling on the route is the other half: it stops one host hammering the endpoint, this stops one account filing against a hundred different people from a hundred hosts. |
| `REPORT_MAX_OPEN` | optional | integer | `5` | How many of one account's reports may sit unreviewed at once. A quota limits the rate; this limits the standing backlog, so a single reporter cannot occupy the queue while moderators work through it. |
| `REPORT_DISMISSED_COOLDOWN_DAYS` | optional | integer | `30` | After a moderator dismisses a report, how long before the same reporter may file about the same person again. Without it, "dismissed" is a round trip: refile, and the queue carries the same complaint for ever. |
| `REPORT_BRIGADING_THRESHOLD` | optional | integer | `5` | How many open reports by distinct accounts against one user make the queue say "this looks coordinated". A flag for a human, never an automatic action: acting on a count is precisely what a brigade is buying. |
| `POST_MAX_PER_DAY` | optional | integer | `20` | Per-account daily ceilings on what one user can put in front of everyone else. The per-IP limits on the routes have the same holes "Report abuse ceilings" describes, and a feed is a worse place to flood than a moderation queue: every other user reads it. Counted only on posts and comments that were actually written. |
| `COMMENT_MAX_PER_DAY` | optional | integer | `200` | Per-account daily ceilings on what one user can put in front of everyone else. The per-IP limits on the routes have the same holes "Report abuse ceilings" describes, and a feed is a worse place to flood than a moderation queue: every other user reads it. Counted only on posts and comments that were actually written. |
| `REMOVED_CONTENT_RETENTION_DAYS` | optional | integer | `30` | How long a post or comment a moderator removed is kept before `purge-removed-content` deletes it. Removal is a status, not a delete, so an appeal can restore it — and this is how long an appeal has. What the author deletes themselves goes at once. |
| `MAX_SUSPENSION_DAYS` | optional | integer | `365` | Longest suspension `PUT /users/{id}/suspend` will set. Past this the honest action is a permanent ban, chosen deliberately rather than arrived at by typing a large number of days. |
| `ADMIN_USER_IDS` | optional | JSON | `[]` | Administrators named by the environment. With OFFICIAL_USER_IDS and the accounts promoted from the app (tb_19) they are what core/roles.isAdmin lets through the admin routes; these are the ones the app cannot revoke. Empty by default. |
| `OFFICIAL_USER_IDS` | optional | JSON | `[]` | UIDs of NoHarm's own accounts — the ones that speak for the app. They carry the "Official" mark, may message anyone, are admins, and alone may promote or demote other admins (core/roles.py). Empty by default. |
| `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS` | optional | integer | `240` | Global IP floor. Per-route slowapi limits are the real ceilings. |
| `RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS` | optional | integer | `60` | Global IP floor. Per-route slowapi limits are the real ceilings. |
| `RATE_LIMIT_BLOCK_SECONDS` | optional | integer | `60` | Global IP floor. Per-route slowapi limits are the real ceilings. |
| `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_BLOCK_SECONDS` | optional | integer | `900` | Global IP floor. Per-route slowapi limits are the real ceilings. |

## Read outside config.py (11)

| Variable | Read by | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `APP_ENV` | config.py, entrypoint.sh | Which `.secrets.toml` section Dynaconf loads: `dev`, `alembic` or `prod`. **Defaults to `prod`** — unset or misspelled silently targets production. |
| `BIND_HOST` | run.py | Address uvicorn binds. Default `127.0.0.1` (behind nginx, the only peer), `0.0.0.0` when `DEBUG` is on. Dev compose sets it so a published port reaches the app. |
| `DATABASE_ENCRYPTION_KEY_OLD` | jobs/rotateEncryptionKey.py | Only for `rotate-encryption-key`: the key being rotated away from. See `operations.md`, "Rotating the column encryption key". |
| `DATABASE_HOST_UNPOOLED` | entrypoint.sh | Host for the composed `DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED` (migrations), when it differs from `DATABASE_HOST` (a pooler in front). Defaults to `DATABASE_HOST`. |
| `DATABASE_PORT` | entrypoint.sh | Port used when the entrypoint composes `DATABASE_URL` from parts. Default 5432. |
| `DATABASE_SSLMODE` | entrypoint.sh | Appended to the composed database URLs as `sslmode=` when set (RDS). |
| `FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_HOST` | firebase-admin, entrypoint.sh | **Test and dev only.** Makes firebase-admin skip ID-token signature checks — anyone can authenticate as anyone. The production entrypoint refuses to start with it set. |
| `PUBLIC_HOSTNAMES` | entrypoint.sh | Comma-separated host names nginx answers on :443 (and redirects from :80); any other `Host` gets 444. Unset answers every host. Only with `TLS_MODE=container`. |
| `RUN_MIGRATIONS` | entrypoint.sh | `true` runs `alembic upgrade head` before serving. Default `false`: migrations are a separate step (`<image> migrate`) so several instances never race the same upgrade. |
| `TLS_MODE` | entrypoint.sh | `alb` (default: plain :80 behind a load balancer) or `container` (nginx terminates TLS; the live instance). Picks the nginx server template. |
| `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` | entrypoint.sh | Required with `TLS_MODE=alb`: the CIDRs allowed to set `X-Forwarded-For` (the VPC range). Anything wider hands the header back to the caller. |

## Front-end build variables

The `VITE_*` values are the front end's, inlined into the bundle at build
time; they are listed in `noHarm/README.md`, "Environment variables", and
passed as build args by `docker/Dockerfile`, `docker/deploy-host.sh` and
`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`.
